rv.q: This is a production stuffed with personality, spectacle and wow factor.
It somehow snatches victory from the jaws of defeat
Todrick Hall's production has more vim than that other recently arrived contender in the hen party stakes, The Devil Wears Prada.
The upshot is rambling raunch, musical cliche and automated whooping.
But all the changes only make Burlesque all the more irresistible.
It might be skimpy, but it covers all the bases it needs to.
This is a noisy, fun show that actually stands head and shoulders above the source material.
Someone has finally found her an answer
Everyone else should approach with extreme caution.

But the Burlesque musical does not project the chaos of its production – running at two hours fifty minutes, it feels pacey, high-octane, and often funny, and is more slathered than sprinkled with incredibly eye-catching performances.

Film fans may find Hall’s expanded creative control as director, writer and choreographer both ambitious and distancing from the original emotional core, resulting in a bold reinvention rather than a faithful celebration.
The production boasts so much potential, and it is evident it is a pure labour of love; however, sadly, the production falls flat on more than one account.
There is some really good material in the show, but it doesn't feel sure what it is supposed to be.
Everything feels like it has been done better elsewhere.
...decidedly un-snappy Burlesque, which spends three hours borrowing shamelessly and tediously from far-superior sources to arrive at an artistic dead end.
